instruction: I'm concerned about online tracking. Can you enable the 'Do Not Track' feature in Chrome to request websites not track my browsing?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"enable_do_not_track":false}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable Do Not Track feature in Chrome settings. The evaluator uses existing get_enable_do_not_track getter to check enable_do_not_track field in Chrome Preferences. Initial state: false. Expected state: true.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_enable_do_not_track reads Chrome Preferences file and correctly extracts the enable_do_not_track field
Metric comparison is correct: exact_match properly compares the string result ('true'/'false') with expected value ('true')
Expected value is semantically correct: Task requires enabling Do Not Track, so expecting 'true' is correct
Complete coverage: Evaluator checks the single requirement (enable Do Not Track) specified in the instruction
State is accessible: Chrome Preferences file is persistent and readable after task completion
Postconfig is appropriate: Restarting Chrome ensures preference changes are saved and can be reliably read
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts boolean -> converts to string -> metric compares with expected string
